items.title: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, joining the frontier in...
items.content:
SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, joining the frontier in line with GPT-5.6 Sol, with standout agentic performance at lower cost

Grok 4.6 gains 5 points over Grok 4.5 on the Intelligence Index just over one month after its release, or +23 points compared to Grok 4.3. This brings SpaceXAI back to the intelligence frontier alongside OpenAI, behind only Anthropic.

Key takeaways:
➤ Grok 4.6 joins the frontier of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: It scores 61, in line with GPT-5.6 Sol (max), behind Claude Opus 5 (max, 63) and Claude Fable 5 (max with fallback, 62), and just ahead of Kimi K3

➤ Strong agentic performance: Grok 4.6 achieves a GDPval-AA v2 Elo of 1753, behind only Claude Opus 5 and with overlapping confidence intervals with Claude Fable 5 and Qwen3.8 Max. It scores 50.7% on 𝜏³-Banking, among the top two scores alongside Qwen3.8 Max (51.3%), and 88.4% on Terminal-Bench v2.1, in line with the leading models

➤ Frontier-level intelligence at lower cost: Headline pricing is unchanged from Grok 4.5 at $2/$6 per 1M input/output tokens, 60%+ below Claude Opus 5 ($5/$25) and GPT-5.6 Sol ($5/$30). It cost $0.84 per task, the same as Kimi K3 with slightly higher intelligence, placing it on the Intelligence vs. Cost per Task Pareto frontier

➤ Grok 4.6 sits at Fable 5-tier on AA-Briefcase, our private benchmark of long-horizon agentic knowledge work tasks, with an Elo of 1577 - behind the Claude Opus 5 family. It is notably turn-efficient, completing tasks in ~53 turns and ~0.5B input tokens on average vs. ~103 turns and ~2.0B input tokens for Claude Opus 5 (max)

Other model details:
➤ Context window of 500k tokens (unchanged from Grok 4.5)

➤ Pricing of $2/$6 per 1M tokens of input/output; cache hits discounted to $0.5 per 1M tokens, an increase over Grok 4.5’s $0.3 per 1M tokens for cache hits

Congratulations to @SpaceXAI and @elonmusk on the release!

items.title: A few years ago, when I started my AI textbook, I would've guessed AI models would've maybe made it ...
items.content:
A few years ago, when I started my AI textbook, I would've guessed AI models would've maybe made it irrelevant at the time of publishing (now in 2026) due to them getting way better at a fairly simple task. I was surprised to be wrong.

Today, models haven't gotten much better at non-fiction/technical writing in long-form. This has me worried for AI models' abilities to do genuine open-ended science, one of the core posited benefits of models. Yes, the models can solve known math problems etc. and make awesome connections across fields, but how are they going to build a literature themselves without massively increasing entropy? Being able to write and organize thoughts is crucial to advancing collective knowledge.

I’m sharing how I came to be worried about this in my latest piece on AI & writing.

items.title: Korean AI lab Upstage has released Solar Pro 4, scoring 42 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence I...
items.content:
Korean AI lab Upstage has released Solar Pro 4, scoring 42 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a significant increase from Solar Pro 3’s 14

Solar Pro 4 is @upstageai's new proprietary flagship reasoning model, replacing Solar Pro 3 from April 2026. At 42 on the Intelligence Index it sits alongside Inkling (xhigh, 42) and just behind MiMo-V2.5-Pro (43), and shows a 27-point increase over Solar Pro 3. Pricing increases to $0.30/$1.20/$0.06 per 1M input/output/cache hit tokens from Solar Pro 3's $0.15/$0.60/$0.02 via Upstage’s first-party API.

Key results:

➤ Solar Pro 4’s largest improvements on Solar Pro 3 are on agentic and long context work. Terminal-Bench v2.1 improves from 12% to 57%, AA-LCR from 31% to 71%, and τ³-Banking from 9% to 23%. GDPval-AA v2 shows strong progress on real-world agentic tasks, where Solar Pro 3 scored an Elo of 498, well below the human baseline of 1000, Solar Pro 4 scores 1276.

➤ AA-Omniscience improvement from -53 to -1 was driven by abstaining on more questions. Solar Pro 4 attempts only 41% of questions against 92% for Solar Pro 3, and its hallucination rate is 24%, higher than Command A+ (14%) and MiniMax-M3 (18%), and a vast improvement from Solar Pro 3’s 88%. AA-Omniscience Accuracy remains unchanged at 19%.

➤ Solar Pro 4 is more token efficient than Solar Pro 3, though still verbose for its intelligence level. It uses 43k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, around 17% fewer than Solar Pro 3's 52k.

➤ The intelligence gain comes with a hit to latency. Solar Pro 4 takes 9.5 minutes to complete an average Intelligence Index task, against 6.9 minutes for Solar Pro 3, despite using fewer output tokens per task.

➤ Pricing is $0.30/$1.20 per 1M input/output tokens. This is in line with @MiniMax_AI's first-party pricing for MiniMax-M3, which scores 3 points higher at 45, and is more expensive than @deepseek_ai's DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort) at $0.14/$0.28 and 52 on the Intelligence Index. Cache hits are priced at $0.06 per 1M, an 80% discount on input token price.

Additional model details:

➤ Context window: 512K tokens

➤ Max output tokens: 128K

➤ Modalities: Text input and output only

➤ Pricing: $0.30 / $1.20 / $0.06 per 1M input/output/cache hit tokens

➤ Inference providers at time of launch: Upstage first-party API, OpenRouter, TimelyRouter

items.content:
We wrote a 36-page ArXiv whitepaper on ExtractBench 🧑‍🔬 , our effort to create the most comprehensive, schema-guided, real-world document extraction benchmark.

It’s extremely detailed and covers everything from comparisons with related work on document extraction, to the dataset construction / how ground-truth is generated, to our experiments over 14+ extraction systems.

Here are some of the most salient points from the paper:
✅ The benchmark scores schema-guided extraction on real enterprise documents. Given input doc + schema and predicted output from an extractor, the benchmark measures value accuracy, grounding, tags for each “challenge”, and cost.
✅ Compared to other benchmarks, we have more schemas, more evaluation dimensions, and more data domain diversity
✅ The ground-truth is constructed according to 3 doc subtypes: real-docs use a model ensemble + human review, synthetic long lists have ground-truth by construction, and scanned forms also have human review incl. boxes
✅ Our three modes (LlamaParse cost-effective, agentic, and agentic plus) are at the Pareto frontier of accuracy and cost.

The full ArXiv paper is here: https://t.co/s5azzQV8zr

Our site: https://t.co/VapjcfKCc3

items.title: LLM training is reaching a point where adding more compute is easier than finding equally good new t...
items.content:
LLM training is reaching a point where adding more compute is easier than finding equally good new text, while the usual “scaling laws”—empirical formulas that predict how training improves as models and datasets grow—largely assume fresh data can keep increasing with compute.

The authors of this recent preprint from @Harvard and @MIT develop a scaling law for the more realistic case where a fixed dataset is supplemented by reused or paraphrased text, introducing a quantity that measures how much each such derived token counts compared with a genuinely new token.

Their experiments show that this value is not fixed: repeated or paraphrased data becomes less useful as more of it is added, and the point of diminishing returns depends on both model size and how much fresh data the model already has.

This leads to a useful picture of training as being limited mainly by compute, fresh data, or model size, and gives concrete predictions for when further training, more data, or a larger model is the better use of resources.

items.content:
In a new study, we asked experts and superforecasters to forecast the effectiveness of @AnthropicAI's AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) safeguards at mitigating biosecurity risks from general-purpose AI (GPAI) models.

To investigate expert and superforecaster views on the effectiveness of ASL-3 at mitigating biosecurity risks, we conducted a forecasting survey (funded by Anthropic PBC) in which respondents had access to information about Anthropic's ASL-3 standards as well as confidential data from red-teaming efforts, the bug bounty program, and other safeguard testing.

Key findings:

• Experts and superforecasters generally believe that implementing ASL-3 safeguards across all GPAI models could substantially reduce the risk of a large-scale human-caused outbreak.

• Forecasters estimate that implementing ASL-3 safeguards across all GPAI models would capture most of the risk reduction it's possible to achieve via safeguarding.

• Protecting all frontier models would substantially reduce risk, but not as much as extending ASL-3 safeguards to all GPAI models would.

• Making jailbreaks harder to find, patching them faster, or further degrading the performance of jailbroken models were generally expected to improve ASL-3 performance, with faster patching thought to be the most effective.

items.title: Kellanova, the company that makes Pringles in Europe, spent four years and roughly $5M working with ...
items.content:
Kellanova, the company that makes Pringles in Europe, spent four years and roughly $5M working with Siemens to build a real time digital twin of its potato chip dough at a factory in Poland. 

The problem it solves is variability. More than 200 parameters affect the final chip, from flour particle size to the humidity of the dough to where and when the potatoes were harvested, and workers previously corrected for all of it by hand and by feel. 

Now sensors capture 200 data points every millisecond and feed a machine learning model that recommends recipe adjustments before problems appear. 

A human operator still approves each change. The line has seen 13 percent less waste, 7 percent lower energy use and a 10 percent capacity gain. 

Digital twins have been a concept in manufacturing for years, but this is what it looks like when one finally starts paying for itself.

Why do so many AI-powered phone agents sound smart until you interrupt them?

Even when these agents...
items.content:
Why do so many AI-powered phone agents sound smart until you interrupt them?

Even when these agents give you reasonable answers, you still leave these calls feeling like you spoke with a machine that was reading one sentence at a time.

We still haven't built voice agents that feel real.

The problem is that traditional text-to-speech treats every line the agent generates as a separate job.

TTS models don't retain the tone, pacing, or context of the sentence that came before.

That's why voice AI is still so awkward.

Deepgram just released Flux TTS to solve this problem:

Flux TTS is a streaming, conversation-native voice model with a single goal: To retain context across agent turns, so your conversation can stay responsive, consistent, and feel natural.

From what I can gather, there are 3 highlights:

1. Flux TTS remembers the conversation and carries tone, pacing, and context across different turns.

2. It streams in real time with latency as low as 80ms.

3. It handles interruptions and can resume naturally after you cut in.

If you are building a voice agent, check out Flux TTS to help your agent maintain context and respond more naturally throughout a conversation:

https://t.co/ysTbsUerP3

Thanks to the @DeepgramAI team for partnering with me on this post.

We surveyed 22 biosecurity, national security, and/or terrorism experts, plus 20 superforecasters.

We asked participants to forecast the total damages attributable to a human-caused disease outbreak that causes at least $100 million in damages between April 2026 and the end of 2028 in four scenarios:

1) A world without general-purpose AI (GPAI)

2) A world where no safeguards are applied to any GPAI model

3) A world where all GPAI models are protected by Anthropic's ASL-3 safeguards

4) A world where only "frontier" GPAI models are protected by ASL-3 safeguards

We asked respondents to assume that AI model capabilities stay fixed at the level of Claude Opus 4.6, to understand views on ASL-3’s effectiveness at mitigating risks from current models.

We can put this in terms of the share of GPAI-attributable risk mitigated by each ASL-3 scenario, since we also asked forecasters to estimate the biosecurity risk in a world without GPAI.

In the chart below, you can see that forecasters estimate that ASL-3 for all models would mitigate 71.7% of GPAI-attributable risk.

One caveat: The "no-GPAI" scenario is an imperfect proxy for perfect safeguards, since such a scenario removes the defensive benefits of GPAI, such as contributions to pandemic surveillance and vaccine development. Thus, this 71.7% efficacy figure is likely biased upward.

items.content:
18 two-word AI prompts I'm kind of obsessed with:

1) now what - great for when you've wrapped up a project or big push and you still have energy and want AI to give you more

2) plz fix - usually accompanied with a screenshot flagging an issue or error or a DM with a bug report

3) do this - usually accompanied with a photo or a screenshot, if I see a great tweet that I want to implement, i'll just screenshot it and toss it to codex/claude

4) interview me - I'm a context hunter, and I want AI to keep pulling more context out of me that I didn't think to first give it, very helpful for tailoring responses or solutions

5) keep going! - I don't know, guys. I just find myself motivating my AI agents a lot more these days. Other versions of this include 'have fun' and 'I trust you'

6) elii elie - this is my shorthand for "explain it to me like I'm an intern" and "explain it to me like I'm an executive" and it's really helpful to get quick reframes if I'm stuck 

7) first principles? - sometimes I read an answer and think 'hmmm that's factually right, but it lacks heart and no one will care' and it's usually because the problem-solving wasn't upstream enough, this prompt helps reset that and reset assumptions

8) simulate it - love when AI runs scenarios, plans for edge cases, and visualizes it all into a dynamic interface for me, this is one of my favorites

9) challenge me - or 'challenge this', used when I desperately need a sparring partner and not a sycophantic kiss-ass :) helps to get a new perspective

10) da fuq? - Fable 5 took a different English class than I did because sometimes that model gives me five paragraphs of hyperdense phd-level info and I'm more lost than when we started

11) find leverage - show me the small moves that create disproportionate outcomes because I don’t always have time to optimize the 37 tiny things

12) hey simon - he's my AI chief of staff, and when I talk directly to him, he can route to and coordinate with the other 33 agents, this is the ultimate 'summoner'

13) spawn agents - any time I'm dealing with massive quantity (like tons of tasks or a lengthy spreadsheet or something), I aim for parallelization. dynamic workflows in claude is another great option 

14) automate this - many times, after a long conversation with AI, I realize that I will need to do that task a whole lot more. So I type something like 'automate this' or 'codify this' or 'schedule this' so it can become a repeatable pattern

15) remember this - any time I flag a mistake or critical context, I'm forcing the AI to log it into memory. It often does it automatically, but not always!

16) forecast impact - asks AI to play out the downstream consequences (including legal, PR, economic, political, team) of whatever I'm asking 

17) show receipts - I want to see solid sources, evidence, reasoning, so I can quickly call out issues (bad sources is a 'fail', and great sources are not an immediate 'pass')

18) girl bye - when AI loses its mind, and I need to get the heck out of there and start a new thread

items.content:
Skyr is minimally processed

I recommend using the NOVA scale, it's a great way to figure out if your food is clean or not, and essentially if you should be eating or not

Just take a pic and ask AI what NOVA scale your food is

I generally flat out avoid eating from groups 3 and 4 nowadays (except cheat days once in a while ;))

What's interesting is that a lot of the food that used to be NOVA 1 (unprocessed) a few decades ago has now become NOVA 4 (ultra processed) due to inflation

The reason is that unprocessed food is cheap and boring and hard to market, so you can't make much profit on it. A steak is a steak and it costs roughly the same everywhere. But if you sell it as 

Grill Masters Sweet & Smoky BBQ Angus Beef

You can add a beautifully designed label, market it in ads, and all the stuff you add it (salt water, coloring, additives) to increase the weight, so you can charge much more

Selling ultra processed food is a much better business to be in than selling unprocessed food (boring and no profit margin)

Thank capitalism for this!

An example is a type of meat my parents used to eat in the Netherlands, it was unprocessed then, and is now sold as ultra processed full of preservatives, emulsifiers, coloring and additives, and my parents have no idea because it looks roughly the same. It makes them sick though

Also yogurt, I grew up and it was just you know, yogurt, fermented milk, classified as NOVA 1 unprocessed. But modern yogurt isn't that anymore. A premium brand I used to buy called OIKOS by Danone, used to have 2 ingredients: milk and fermentation bacteria. Now it's some milk, a bit of cream, a lot of milk powder (with dubious origins) and fermentation bacteria to save money but the price went up! And that's the plain one. The flavored yogurts are full of artificial sweeteners, emulsifiers, additives etc.

So you can't really trust your eyes anymore to judge if food is clean or not, because most of it has been turned into processed or ultra processed to save money and/or market to you to sell for a higher price

When in doubt, try the NOVA scale

This is not only a problem for tech companies.

Consider hospitals running clinical decision agents. Manufacturers operating predictive maintenance loops. Logistics hubs routing shipments through autonomous models. Financial services firms processing compliance workflows with no human in the loop.

Every one of these environments faces the same underlying challenge:

→ Data that is not governed at agent speed

→ Networks not designed for GPU communication patterns

→ Workloads placed on cost assumptions built for pilots, not persistence

→ Governance designed for the prompt layer — not the infrastructure layer 

HPE and NVIDIA are addressing these gaps through HPE AI Factory with NVIDIA enterprise reference architectures built for production scale. The architecture gap is not theoretical. It is operational.

items.content:
People asked if this meal is nutritionally complete, how on earth can you get all the nutrients you need from just this meal?

Well yes you can if you add some more things:
- Skyr (protein, calcium, B12, probiotics) with cinnamon, squeezed lemon juice and strawberries (vitamin C + fiber + polyphenols)
- Brussels sprouts (vitamin C + fiber + beneficial sulfur)
- Sunlight (go walk or sit outside for vitamin D ~15-30 min in late afternoon at low UV index)

The rest is already there:
- Steak (protein for muscle repair + strength, iron, zinc, B12, CoQ10, 
- 20g/day of 92% dark chocolate (flavanols, antioxidants, minerals, healthy fats)
- Black coffee (caffeine, antioxidants, lowers risk of cancer)
- 2 bananas (pottasium, natural carbs, fiber, B6)

Only thing missing here would be omega-3 from fish or eggs!
